method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); the date arithmetic in one module, the rules in another, the questions in a seat module importing them; one regulative rule (s 33ZA(3)(c)) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain dates; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Federal Court of Australia Act 1976 (Cth), Compilation No. 59 (compilation date 11 December 2024, register id C2024C00819), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A01586.txt, retrieved 2026-10-13; with the Federal Court Rules 2011, Compilation No. 11 (11 June 2026, register id F2026C00512), rr 1.61(2), (5), 9.33, 9.34, 36.03, as deposited at subjects/au/federal-court-rules-2011/registers/source-bundle/F2011L01551.txt, retrieved 2026-11-06. Amendments after the compilation dates are not in the texts.

checks.command: l4 run fca4a-dates.l4 ; l4 run fca4a-rules.l4 ; l4 run fca4a-seat.l4 ; l4 run fca4a-cases.l4

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.
